# Problem 1 - OOP Programming

## (a) Defining the waldCI Class

```{r}
setClass(
  "waldCI",
  slots = c(
    estimate = "numeric",
    sterr = "numeric",
    level = "numeric",
    lower = "numeric",
    upper = "numeric"
  )
)

```

```{r}
#' Validate a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param object A waldCI object
#' @return TRUE if valid, otherwise an error message
setValidity("waldCI", function(object) {
  lengths <- c(
    length(object@estimate),
    length(object@sterr),
    length(object@level),
    length(object@lower),
    length(object@upper)
  )

  if (any(lengths != 1)) {
    return("All slots must contain exactly one value.")
  }

  values <- c(
    object@estimate,
    object@sterr,
    object@level,
    object@lower,
    object@upper
  )

  if (any(!is.finite(values))) {
    return("All values must be finite.")
  }

  if (object@sterr < 0) {
    return("Standard error must be nonnegative.")
  }

  if (object@level <= 0 || object@level >= 1) {
    return("Confidence level must be between 0 and 1.")
  }

  if (object@lower > object@upper) {
    return("Lower bound cannot exceed upper bound.")
  }

  z <- qnorm((1 - object@level) / 2, lower.tail = FALSE)

  expected <- object@estimate + c(-1, 1) * z * object@sterr

  if (any(!is.finite(expected))) {
    return("The implied confidence bounds must be finite.")
  }

  actual <- c(object@lower, object@upper)

  if (!isTRUE(all.equal(actual, expected, tolerance = 1e-10))) {
    return("Confidence bounds are inconsistent with the estimate and standard error.")
  }

  TRUE
})

```

```{r}
#' Construct a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param level Confidence level between 0 and 1
#' @param mean Point estimate, if supplied
#' @param sterr Standard error, if supplied
#' @param lb Lower confidence bound, if supplied
#' @param ub Upper confidence bound, if supplied
#' @return A validated waldCI object
makeWaldCI <- function(level, mean = NULL, sterr = NULL,
                       lb = NULL, ub = NULL) {

  if (!is.numeric(level) || length(level) != 1 ||
      !is.finite(level) || level <= 0 || level >= 1) {
    stop("Confidence level must be a finite number between 0 and 1.")
  }

  from_stats <- !is.null(mean) && !is.null(sterr) &&
    is.null(lb) && is.null(ub)

  from_bounds <- !is.null(lb) && !is.null(ub) &&
    is.null(mean) && is.null(sterr)

  if (!from_stats && !from_bounds) {
    stop("Supply either mean and sterr, or lb and ub.")
  }

  z <- qnorm((1 - level) / 2, lower.tail = FALSE)

  if (from_stats) {
    if (!is.numeric(mean) || length(mean) != 1 ||
        !is.finite(mean)) {
      stop("Mean must be a single finite number.")
    }

    if (!is.numeric(sterr) || length(sterr) != 1 ||
        !is.finite(sterr) || sterr < 0) {
      stop("Standard error must be a single nonnegative finite number.")
    }

    lb <- mean - z * sterr
    ub <- mean + z * sterr
  }

  if (from_bounds) {
    if (!is.numeric(lb) || length(lb) != 1 ||
        !is.finite(lb) ||
        !is.numeric(ub) || length(ub) != 1 ||
        !is.finite(ub)) {
      stop("Confidence bounds must be finite numbers.")
    }

    if (lb > ub) {
      stop("Lower bound cannot exceed upper bound.")
    }

    mean <- (lb + ub) / 2
    sterr <- (ub - lb) / (2 * z)
  }

  object <- new(
    "waldCI",
    estimate = as.numeric(mean),
    sterr = as.numeric(sterr),
    level = as.numeric(level),
    lower = as.numeric(lb),
    upper = as.numeric(ub)
  )

  validObject(object)

  return(object)
}

```

```{r}
#' Display a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param object A waldCI object
#' @return The object, invisibly
setMethod("show", "waldCI", function(object) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "%.1f%% Wald confidence interval: [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
    100 * object@level,
    object@lower,
    object@upper
  ))

  cat(sprintf(
    "Estimate: %.4f\nStandard error: %.4f\n",
    object@estimate,
    object@sterr
  ))

  invisible(object)
})

```

```{r}
#' Update the lower bound of a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param object A waldCI object
#' @param value New lower confidence bound
#' @return A validated waldCI object
setMethod("lb<-", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
  return(makeWaldCI(
    level = object@level,
    lb = value,
    ub = object@upper
  ))
})

#' Update the upper bound of a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param object A waldCI object
#' @param value New upper confidence bound
#' @return A validated waldCI object
setMethod("ub<-", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
  return(makeWaldCI(
    level = object@level,
    lb = object@lower,
    ub = value
  ))
})

#' Update the standard error of a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param object A waldCI object
#' @param value New standard error
#' @return A validated waldCI object
setMethod("sterr<-", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
  return(makeWaldCI(
    level = object@level,
    mean = object@estimate,
    sterr = value
  ))
})

#' Update the confidence level of a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param object A waldCI object
#' @param value New confidence level
#' @return A validated waldCI object
setMethod("level<-", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
  return(makeWaldCI(
    level = value,
    mean = object@estimate,
    sterr = object@sterr
  ))
})

#' Update the estimate of a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param x A waldCI object
#' @param value New point estimate
#' @return A validated waldCI object
setMethod("mean<-", "waldCI", function(x, value) {
  return(makeWaldCI(
    level = x@level,
    mean = value,
    sterr = x@sterr
  ))
})
```

```{r}
#' Check whether a value is within a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param object A waldCI object
#' @param value A numeric value
#' @return A logical indicating whether the value is within the interval
setGeneric("contains", function(object, value) {
  standardGeneric("contains")
})

#' Check whether two Wald confidence intervals overlap
#'
#' @param x A waldCI object
#' @param y Another waldCI object
#' @return A logical indicating whether the intervals overlap
setGeneric("overlap", function(x, y) {
  standardGeneric("overlap")
})

#' Transform a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param object A waldCI object
#' @param fun A monotonic transformation function
#' @return A transformed waldCI object
setGeneric("transformCI", function(object, fun) {
  standardGeneric("transformCI")
})

```

```{r}
#' Determine whether a value is inside a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param object A waldCI object
#' @param value A numeric value
#' @return TRUE if the value is within the interval, otherwise FALSE
setMethod("contains", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
  if (!is.numeric(value) || length(value) != 1 ||
      !is.finite(value)) {
    stop("Value must be a single finite number.")
  }

  return(value >= object@lower && value <= object@upper)
})

#' Determine whether two Wald confidence intervals overlap
#'
#' @param x A waldCI object
#' @param y Another waldCI object
#' @return TRUE if the intervals overlap, otherwise FALSE
setMethod(
  "overlap",
  signature(x = "waldCI", y = "waldCI"),
  function(x, y) {
    return(x@lower <= y@upper && y@lower <= x@upper)
  }
)

```

```{r}
#' Convert a Wald confidence interval to a numeric vector
#'
#' @param x A waldCI object
#' @param ... Additional arguments
#' @return A numeric vector containing the lower and upper bounds
setMethod("as.numeric", "waldCI", function(x, ...) {
  return(c(x@lower, x@upper))
})

```

```{r}
#' Transform a Wald confidence interval using a monotonic function
#'
#' @param object A waldCI object
#' @param fun A function monotonic over the confidence interval
#' @return A validated transformed waldCI object
setMethod("transformCI", "waldCI", function(object, fun) {
  if (!is.function(fun)) {
    stop("The transformation must be a function.")
  }

  warning(
    "Only monotonic functions make sense for transforming confidence intervals.",
    call. = FALSE
  )

  transformed <- c(
    fun(object@lower),
    fun(object@upper)
  )

  if (!is.numeric(transformed) || length(transformed) != 2 ||
      any(!is.finite(transformed))) {
    stop("The transformed bounds must be finite numeric values.")
  }

  bounds <- sort(transformed)

  return(makeWaldCI(
    level = object@level,
    lb = bounds[1],
    ub = bounds[2]
  ))
})

```

## (b) Creating and Evaluating Wald Confidence Intervals

```{r}
ci1 <- makeWaldCI(
  level = 0.95,
  lb = 17.2,
  ub = 24.7
)

ci2 <- makeWaldCI(
  level = 0.99,
  mean = 13,
  sterr = 2.5
)

  ub = 39.22
)
```

## (c) Testing the Validator

```{r}
invalid_sterr <- ci1
invalid_sterr@sterr <- -1
validObject(invalid_sterr, test = TRUE)

invalid_bounds <- ci1
invalid_bounds@lower <- 30
validObject(invalid_bounds, test = TRUE)

invalid_infinite <- ci1
invalid_infinite@upper <- Inf
validObject(invalid_infinite, test = TRUE)

```

```{r}
tryCatch(
  makeWaldCI(level = 0.95, mean = 10, sterr = -1),
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)

tryCatch(
  makeWaldCI(level = 0.95, lb = 30, ub = 20),
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)

tryCatch(
  makeWaldCI(level = 0.95, lb = 10, ub = Inf),
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)

```

```{r}
setter_test <- ci1

tryCatch(
  { lb(setter_test) <- 30 },
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)

tryCatch(
  { ub(setter_test) <- 10 },
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)

tryCatch(
  { mean(setter_test) <- Inf },
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)

tryCatch(
  { sterr(setter_test) <- -1 },
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)

tryCatch(
  { level(setter_test) <- 1.2 },
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)

validObject(setter_test)
as.numeric(setter_test)

```

The results confirm that the validator correctly identifies negative standard errors, lower bounds exceeding upper bounds, and infinite confidence bounds. The constructor also rejects these invalid inputs, and all five setters prevent invalid modifications. After the unsuccessful setter operations, the original confidence interval remains valid, with its bounds unchanged at $[17.2, 24.7]$.

# Problem 2 - data.table

## (a) Number of Tournaments in 2019

```{r}
library(data.table)

tennis <- fread("data/atp_matches_2019.csv")

dim(tennis)
names(tennis)

```

```{r}
tennis[, .(n_tournaments = uniqueN(tourney_id))]

```
There were **128 tournaments** in 2019, counting each unique `tourney_id` as a separate tournament.

\

## (b) Players with Multiple Tournament Titles

```{r}
champions <- tennis[
  round == "F",
  .(tourney_id, winner_id, winner_name)
]

title_counts <- champions[
  ,
  .(n_titles = uniqueN(tourney_id)),
  by = .(winner_id, winner_name)
]

multi_winners <- title_counts[
  n_titles > 1
][
  order(-n_titles, winner_name)
]

multi_winners

```

```{r}
multi_winners[
  ,
  .(
    n_players = .N,
    max_titles = max(n_titles)
  )
]

multi_winners[
  n_titles == max(n_titles)
]

```
In 2019, 12 players won more than one tournament. Dominic Thiem and Novak Djokovic tied for the most tournament titles, each winning 5 tournaments.

\

## (c) Comparing Aces Between Winners and Losers

```{r}
ace_data <- tennis[
  !is.na(w_ace) & !is.na(l_ace),
  .(w_ace, l_ace)
]

ace_data[, ace_diff := w_ace - l_ace]

dim(ace_data)

```

```{r}
ace_summary <- ace_data[
  ,
  .(
    n_matches = .N,
    mean_winner_aces = mean(w_ace),
    mean_loser_aces = mean(l_ace),
    mean_diff = mean(ace_diff),
    se_diff = sd(ace_diff) / sqrt(.N)
  )
]

ace_summary[
  ,
  `:=`(
    ci_lower = mean_diff - 1.96 * se_diff,
    ci_upper = mean_diff + 1.96 * se_diff
  )
]

ace_summary

```

After excluding matches with missing ace statistics, 2,694 matches remained for analysis. Winners averaged 7.50 aces per match, compared with 5.79 for losers.

Using the paired differences between winners' and losers' ace counts, the mean difference was 1.70 aces, with an approximate 95% confidence interval of $[1.43, 1.97]$.

Since the entire confidence interval is above zero, there is evidence that winners have more aces than losers on average.

\

## (d) Players with the Highest Win Rate

```{r}
player_results <- rbindlist(list(
  tennis[, .(
    player_id = winner_id,
    player_name = winner_name,
    won = 1L
  )],
  tennis[, .(
    player_id = loser_id,
    player_name = loser_name,
    won = 0L
  )]
))

win_rates <- player_results[
  !is.na(player_id),
  .(
    n_matches = .N,
    n_wins = sum(won),
    win_rate = mean(won)
  ),
  by = .(player_id, player_name)
][
  n_matches >= 5
][
  order(-win_rate, -n_matches, player_name)
]

head(win_rates, 10)

```

```{r}
top_players <- win_rates[
  win_rate == max(win_rate)
]

top_players

```
Among players who participated in at least 5 matches in 2019, **Rafael Nadal had the highest win rate of approximately 86.96%**, winning 60 out of 69 matches. No other player achieved the same win rate.
